title: The final universal-validity reduction omits negation before satisfiable.
details: Logic and Mechanized Reasoning online release 0.1, §12.3, final paragraph before the theorem, accessed 2026-10-21. The sentence asserts that a sentence is valid exactly when its negation is satisfiable. This reverses the reduction: validity is equivalent to unsatisfiability of the negation. For example, a tautology is valid and its negation has no model; falsity is invalid and its negation has a model. The same section earlier states the correct complement relation, and the concluding decidability theorem is correct. The corpus must use the unsatisfiable-negation test explicitly for universal validity. This is a missing logical negation in a mathematical claim, not a missing explanation or a failure of the main theorem.
